statement: Oxygen is the strongest lever on whether a droplet flame goes out by itself: self-extinction is common in oxygen-poor air and rare once oxygen is enriched.
numbers: Tests ending in self-extinction, O2/N2 near 1 atm. Heptane: 11 of 14 at or below 16% O2; 5 of 17 at 20-22% O2; 0 of 3 at 23-30% O2 | Methanol: 22 of 22 at or below 16% O2; 9 of 12 at 20-22% O2; 2 of 4 at 23-30% O2
basis: Counts of FLEX tests (PSI-69) with test end = Extinction; other tests ended in Disruption or Completion. Observed data, not model output.

statement: In the low-pressure, oxygen-enriched conditions closest to proposed exploration atmospheres, no FLEX droplet flame put itself out.
numbers: 0 of 17 tests self-extinguished at 0.70-0.71 atm with 30%-34% O2 in N2 (8 heptane, 9 methanol).
basis: Counts of FLEX tests (PSI-69). Liquid droplets only; says nothing direct about solids.

statement: Fuel burns faster as oxygen rises: going from 21% to 30% O2 at 1 atm raises the burning-rate constant K by about a third.
numbers: Model, 3 mm droplet, 21% -> 30% O2 at 1 atm: Heptane 0.53 -> 0.70 mm2/s (+32%); Methanol 0.50 -> 0.67 mm2/s (+34%). Mean measured K (mm2/s), O2/N2 near 1 atm: Heptane: 0.47 at or below 16% O2, 0.56 at 20-22% O2, 0.74 at 23-30% O2; Methanol: 0.36 at or below 16% O2, 0.50 at 20-22% O2, 0.67 at 23-30% O2.
basis: Ridge model on FLEX (PSI-69), both points inside the data domain, plus measured means.

statement: Adding CO2 slows droplet burning and makes self-extinction more likely; adding helium does not slow burning.
numbers: Tests at 17-21% O2 near 1 atm (mean K in mm2/s). Heptane/N2: K 0.55, self-extinguished 7 of 20; Heptane/CO2: K 0.46, self-extinguished 12 of 18; Heptane/He: K 0.57, self-extinguished 5 of 11; Methanol/N2: K 0.48, self-extinguished 13 of 16; Methanol/CO2: K 0.45, self-extinguished 17 of 19; Methanol/He: K 0.52, self-extinguished 7 of 7.
basis: Grouped FLEX tests (PSI-69). Not a controlled comparison: diluent fraction and exact O2 differ between groups.

statement: Lowering cabin pressure barely changes the chance of self-extinction; the oxygen enrichment that usually comes with it removes most of that chance.
numbers: Model probability of self-extinction, 3 mm droplet in O2/N2. Heptane: 43% at 21% O2/1.0 atm, 41% at 21%/0.7 atm, 2% at 30%/0.7 atm; Methanol: 72% at 21% O2/1.0 atm, 70% at 21%/0.7 atm, 6% at 30%/0.7 atm.
basis: Logistic model on FLEX (PSI-69), all points inside the data domain. Pressure range tested in N2 is mostly 0.7 and 1.0 atm.

statement: When a flame self-extinguishes, unburned fuel is left behind, and for heptane most of the droplet remains.
numbers: Median droplet diameter at visible-flame extinction, as a share of initial diameter: heptane 84% (56 tests), methanol 57% (103 tests).
basis: FLEX tests (PSI-69) ending in Extinction with both diameters recorded. Observed data.
